reasoning: The two attempts make the same code change (the ByName lookup) and give the same verdicts, so the write-ups decide it. A is slightly better in two places. Its pool rejection lists more concrete costs: memory, stale state on reused parts, and replication. Its measurement plan is more specific, naming the ScriptProfiler, Stats.InstanceCount and Stats.DataReceiveKbps with expected values. Its network numbers are also more concrete.

criteria.note: Works out 80 placements/s per server, microseconds each, ~30 bytes per call and ~0.3 KB/s per player, and concludes no item is needed for performance.
Says unreliable events may be dropped or reordered so clicks would silently fail, and notes the client asserts remote:IsA("RemoteEvent").
Pool: blocks never destroyed, plus memory, stale-state reset bugs and replication cost. Buffer: saves about 0.15 KB/s and needs hand-written validation. Native: the work is engine calls.
Removes VALID_NAMES and uses the existing BlockTypes.ByName lookup with an early return. The string type check still runs first, and all the other validation is untouched.

weaknesses: The claim that native code is documented for only some client platforms is loosely worded
